summary: All three blocking findings are valid and require direct spec repair: task input source, broad implementation entrypoint, and safe cursor promotion predicate.

items.title: Task-scoped requirement/file source is undefined
items.rationale: The spec currently requires task-scoped requirements and files without defining a concrete source. That blocks implementation and tests for prompt/context scoping.
items.evidence: spec.json R3 and T-3 mention current task requirements/files, but task schema only contains goal, acceptance, implementation_notes, and test_strategy.

items.title: Broad implementation opt-in has no CLI integration point
items.rationale: Implementation is exposed through next-action run-impl rather than a flow run implement command, so broad implementation needs a defined entrypoint or explicit narrowing.
items.evidence: spec.json R2/R4 include implement in strict/broad mode, while acceptance criteria mention only review and gate broad execution.

items.title: Null cursor recovery predicate conflicts with mid-implementation failure policy
items.rationale: The spec must define the safe boundary for auto-promotion so implementation cannot promote over in-progress or orphaned task state.
items.evidence: spec.json R1 promotes pending tasks when non-terminal tasks exist, while R2 and clarifications require null cursor failure outside dispatcher-owned boundaries.
